title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied-ML evaluation practices for: the eval-harness, prompt set and benchmark catalog, model onboarding checks, quality guardrails, quantization profiles, and regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, SREs responsible for model serving, and product owners who operate production LLM features.

Goals
- Provide a repeatable onboarding path for new models and model variants so they can be served safely across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Define a unified eval and prompt-set standard to reduce false positives/negatives during rollouts.
- Standardize quantization profile evaluation and risk controls.
- Define regression triage and escalation steps with clear owners and SLAs.

Scope
- Applies to all model types used for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking within Redwood services.
- Excludes research-only experiments (those must land in the research repo and then follow onboarding when promoted).

Owner and Roles
- Playbook owner: Applied ML (owner: Priya Singh)
- Eval platform: Eng - Eval Harness team (primary contact: Maya Chen)
- Model review: Applied ML + Model Onboarding committee (members from product, infra, security)
- Incident/Escalation: Eng-SRE (oncall) -> Applied ML lead -> Product PM for customer-impacting regressions

Key Services and Artifacts
- eval-harness (service): automated runner for unit, integration, and regression evals.
- prompt-catalog (repo): canonical prompt sets and benchmark definitions.
- model-registry (service): model metadata, quantization profiles, version pins, and rollout tags.
- quality-dashboard (console): per-model SLOs, eval results, and prompt-level deltas.

Evaluation Standards (minimum checks)
1) Unit Evals (per-model)
- deterministic test prompts: 50 examples covering core functionality and edge cases.
- metrics: accuracy/EM where applicable, BLEU/ROUGE for summarization baselines, and domain-specific correctness checks.
- pass threshold: model must meet baseline >= 95% of the reference model for critical prompts (configurable by product).

2) Safety & Content Guardrails
- Toxicity classifier pass-rate >= 99% (based on internal toxicity harness).
- Sensitive entity redaction/recall checks for regulated verticals (health/finance).
- Reject rate for policy-unsafe prompts must be within expected range from training: if > +2 SD from historical baseline, flag for investigation.

3) Latency & Throughput Profiles
- 95th percentile token latency must be within target for the deployment tier: Hosted <= 500ms, Dedicated <= 350ms, Private depends on customer SLA.
- Perf tests must run under realistic concurrency levels (see "Perf Test Matrix" table below).

Perf Test Matrix
| Model Class | Sequence Lengths (tokens) | Concurrency | Target 95p Latency |
|---|---|---|---|
| small / 7B-class | 128/512 | 50| Hosted: 300ms, Dedicated: 200ms |
| medium / 13B-class | 512/1024 | 30| Hosted: 450ms, Dedicated: 300ms |
| large / 70B+ | 1024/2048 | 10| Hosted: 700ms, Dedicated: 450ms |

Onboarding Checklist (step-by-step)
1. Submit model to model-registry with metadata: architecture, training-corpus summary, license, baseline eval artifact link, and proposed quantization profiles.
2. Run eval-harness onboarding suite: `eval-harness run --model <model-id> --suite onboarding`
3. Confirm unit evals and safety checks pass. If any check fails, document failure reason and remediate before continuing.
4. Run quantization candidate tests (see Quantization section).
5. Submit PR to prompt-catalog if new prompt sets or benchmark adjustments are required. PR must include rationale, example inputs/expected outputs, and reviewers.
6. Schedule a canary rollout: 0.5% traffic for 24 hours with continuous monitoring on quality-dashboard.
7. If canary metrics meet thresholds (no significant regressions in primary prompts, latency within target, and safety checks green), increase to 5% for 24 hours, then 25% for 48 hours, then full rollout.

Canary Rollout SLO Gates
- No single prompt in the primary prompt set increases failure rate by > 2x baseline.
- Overall token-level quality metric (application-specific) must not degrade by > 1.5% relative to baseline.
- No safety policy violations in canary logs.

Quantization Profiles and Evaluation
- Supported profiles: fp16, int8-qat, int8-static, int4-experimental (int4 allowed only for non-sensitive deployments and after explicit approval).
- For each profile run: accuracy delta report, latency/throughput benchmark, memory usage, and KV-cache behavior.
- Quantization candidate command: `model-registry eval-quant --model <id> --profile int8-static --out report.json`
- Pass criteria: accuracy delta <= 1% relative to unquantized baseline for primary prompts AND 90th-percentile latency improvement >= 10% OR memory reduction >= 30% (profile-specific).
- If a profile fails accuracy thresholds, produce a regression ticket and include representative failure prompts.

Prompt Sets and Benchmarking
- Prompt catalog organization: `primary` (user-facing, must be immutable after approval), `secondary` (internal edge cases), `safety` (policy tests), `perf` (for perf-specific sequences).
- Each prompt entry must have: id, description, canonical input, expected output (or scoring rubric), owner, and tags.
- Benchmark runs should annotate and store per-prompt outputs in the eval-harness artifact store for future regression diffing.

Regression Triage Playbook
1) Detection
- Sources: nightly regression runs, canary monitoring alerts, customer incident reports, quality-dashboard anomalies.
- Automated detection thresholds: alert when prompt-level failure delta > 5% absolute or > 2 SD above historical.

2) Initial Triage (15-min SLA for acknowledgement by oncall)
- Validate alert (re-run eval-harness subset).
- Identify impacted model-version(s), prompt set, and customer scope.

3) Root Cause & Mitigation (1-hour target for mitigation plan)
- Check recent changes: model rollout, quantization profile change, runtime kernel upgrades, tokenization changes, prompt modifications.
- Run targeted comparisons: `eval-harness diff --base <baseline-artifact> --head <current-artifact> --prompts <list>`
- Common mitigations: rollback to previous model pin, disable quantization profile, increase canary isolation, or temporary rate-limiting for affected customers.

4) Communication & Escalation
- If customer-impacting: page Eng-SRE, Applied ML lead, and Product PM.
- Create postmortem ticket within 24 hours if not resolved within 8 hours.

5) Postmortem & Prevention
- Document root cause, timeline, and remediation in confluence under `applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage`.
- Action items must include owners, due dates, and verification steps.

Decision Criteria Table (summary)
| Change Type | Required Checks | Required Approvers | Post-change Monitoring |
|---|---|---|---|
| New model family | Full onboarding suite + quantization candidate tests + safety suite | Applied ML committee + Security (if PII) + Product | 7-day elevated canary + daily eval report |
| Model variant (temperature/decoding) | Unit evals + perf sanity | Applied ML owner | 24-72 hour canary |
| Quantization profile enable | Profile evals + accuracy delta analysis | Applied ML + Eng-Perf | 48-hour canary + perf dashboard monitoring |

Operational Playbook Examples
- Example: Resolving a quantization regression
1) Alert: nightly eval shows 3% drop in primary prompt accuracy after enabling int8-static for model-X.
2) Oncall re-runs quant eval and confirms delta.
3) Mitigation: disable int8-static by pinning requests to unquantized model via model-registry and revert runtime config.
4) Root cause: calibration dataset bias; fix: expand calibration set and re-run int8-qat with updated calibration.

CLI and Artifact Examples
- Run onboarding suite:
```
# Run the onboarding suite end-to-end
eval-harness run --model rwd/model-x:v2 --suite onboarding --out artifacts/model-x-onboard-20261214.json
```
- Example quant eval output (JSON summary snippet):
```
{"model":"rwd/model-x:v2","profile":"int8-static","accuracy_delta":"0.012","latency_95p_reduction":"0.18","artifact":"s3://eval-artifacts/model-x/int8-static/report.json"}
```

Monitoring and Dashboards
- Quality-dashboard widgets to configure: per-prompt failure rate, token-quality delta, toxicity incidents, latency percentiles, and canary traffic slices.
- Daily digest: auto-email to Applied ML and Eng-SRE with top 10 prompt regressions and any new safety violations.

C. FAQ
Q: When is int4 allowed in production?
A: Only after explicit Applied ML + Security approval and for low-risk, internal workloads; must pass an extended 14-day canary and additional safety checks.
